# Implementation Plan: an arbiter's tooling fix is made, not lost (feature 379)

**Spec**: `spec.md` | **Request**: `request.md` | **Builds on**: feature 375's round arbiter (`scripts/hooks/lib/hm_arbiter.py`,
`.claude/agents/round-arbiter.md`), the GM's review after landing (`scripts/gm_review.py`) and the closing check
(`scripts/gates/close_check.py`).

## Summary

The ruling gains a `tooling_fix` field; `make arbiter-ruled` records it as an OPEN item on the ruling's row in the feature's
`arbiter.jsonl`, and the ruling's GM-review row carries it. Every `make tick` of that feature, and its closing check, refuse
while one is open. Two commands close it - done (what was built and its test) or declined as an overhaul (why) - and each
adds a row to the GM's review. Tooling only: every task `research: rendering`.

## Constitution Check

I-V N/A (no UI, no pool content, no SOURCE blocks). VI N/A (no generator change). XII N/A (no physical decision). XIII: the
tooling tests and `make hooks-test` green before landing. XIV: none found yet. XVI: built as asked; decisions below.

## Decisions

**D1 - The field, and the contract.** The ruling JSON takes an optional `tooling_fix`: one sentence naming the tool and the
change. The arbiter's contract gives one whenever the loop it judged came from a tooling gap - a guard that let a known
hazard through, a command that misled, a bundle that hid what it needed - and says it is MADE by the session, soon, never
filed. A `process-fault` ruling MUST carry one (its fault, named so a tool can be built against it): `record_ruling` refuses
a `process-fault` without it. The contract's "the fault is filed as a tooling row" becomes "the fault is your
`tooling_fix`"; no ruling's text tells anyone to file a tooling row (FR-001).

**D2 - Recorded open, and shown to the GM.** `record_ruling` keeps `tooling_fix` on the ruling's `arbiter.jsonl` row with
`"fix": "open"`, and on its GM-review row. A later `arbiter.jsonl` row `{"fix_of": "<trigger>", "status": "done"|"declined",
"note": ..., "utc": ...}` closes it; the latest wins. `hm_arbiter.open_fixes(feature dir) -> list[(trigger, tooling_fix)]` is
the one rule every hold reads. The `process-fault` row in `found.jsonl` is no longer written: the open item replaces it
(the found row was what nothing enforced, spec review round 1).

**D3 - The hold is the next tick, and the close.** `scripts/tick-task.py` refuses ANY tick of a feature with an open fix,
naming each and both commands. A tick is the session's next step forward, so the fix is made before the work goes on
("before proceeding with the rest of your implementation") without interrupting a step in flight. `close_check.reasons`
refuses too, so neither a closing status line nor the push closes the feature around it (FR-002, FR-004).

**D4 - Done, with its test, on the GM's review.** `make arbiter-fix-done ID=<trigger> NOTE="<what was built>" TEST=<test
file>`: the TEST must be an existing file under `tests/` (a fix without a test is not done - a guard proves it fires); the
NOTE has the escape reason floor (two words, eight characters). It writes the closing row and a GM-review row (`kind:
arbiter-fix-done`, the fix, the note, the test) and ensures the GM-review box (FR-002).

**D5 - Declined as an overhaul, to the GM.** `make arbiter-fix-declined ID=<trigger> REASON="<why it overhauls a process>"`
(the same floor) writes the closing row and a GM-review row (`kind: arbiter-fix-declined`) and ensures the box (feature 375
FR-012). Nothing files a feature; nothing waits on the GM; the GM reviews it after landing and may overturn it into a
feature (FR-003).

**D6 - The motivating case (SC-001).** 378's ruling in the research clone predates the field; its fix - one gate at a time in
a clone - landed separately today (`scripts/gates/gate_lock.py`). The replay test feeds that ruling, with its fix as the
field, through D2-D5: open; tick refused; close_check refuses; done with `tests/tooling/test_gate_lock.py` closes it and
puts it on the GM's review; a second ruling declined puts the reason there.

**D7 - Where it is written down.** CLAUDE.md's `checks-hooks.sh` guard row gains the hold (one clause); the two targets
carry `##` lines for `make docs`. The guard-file edits (Makefile) carry GUARD_EDIT_OK.

## Amendment 1 - a tooling fix lands alone (FR-005, FR-006)

**D8 - A subset landing, not a flag.** The open-task refusal keeps its "there is no flag" (GM 2026-08-25) and is not
touched: the sessions' deltas mix engine or record work with tooling, so an exemption for an all-tooling delta would never
fire. `make land-tooling FILES="<paths>"` (`scripts/land-tooling.sh`) builds a NEW commit on top of the latest main holding
only those files' changes since the clone's merge base with main (`git diff <merge-base> HEAD -- FILES`, applied with plain
`git apply --index`: a failure IS FR-005's "does not apply cleanly"), in a detached worktree at
`.clones/<clone>-tooling` (a detached worktree is no local branch; the project already uses one for baselines), and lands
that commit with `scripts/sync-with-main.sh done` run from the worktree, so every push check runs unchanged. The clone's
own history is untouched; its next merge of main meets identical hunks and is clean (SC-003). The worktree is removed on
every exit. Measured: `.specify/feature.json` is untracked, so the worktree carries no feature pointer and the open-task
check finds no feature in a delta that touches no `specs/`; `sync-with-main.sh` requires only that its root sit under
`.clones/`.

**D9 - FILES is required and named, never inferred.** A file lands whole, and mid-feature a `CLAUDE.md`, a test or the
`Makefile` edit may describe engine work that has not landed; so with no FILES the command lists the tooling paths the
delta changed and exits 2 (the guard producing the compliant command). A path outside FR-005's set - `scripts/`, `tests/`,
`.claude/agents/`, `.claude/skills/`, any `CLAUDE.md`, the `Makefile`, `.claude/settings.json`, `docs/make-targets.html` -
is refused naming it; so is a FILE with uncommitted changes (only committed work lands). A `Makefile` among them
regenerates `docs/make-targets.html` in the worktree. The checks before the push: `make hooks-test`, `make test-file
FILE=tests/tooling`, and `make test-file` on every test file among FILES (a test needing work not yet landed fails there,
not on main), in the worktree, logged, the tail shown on failure.
The commit is the GM's identity with the clone's commit subjects that touched the files, and the co-author line.

**D10 - Done means landed (FR-006).** `settle_fix(..., "done", ...)` fetches main and refuses unless the TEST file's blob
on `origin/main` equals its blob at the clone's HEAD, naming `make land-tooling FILES="<the test> ..."`. The existing test
fixture gains an `origin/main` holding the test, in the same edit (SC-004).

## Amendment 2 - the arbiter before the GM (FR-007 to FR-010)

**D11 - The spec review's sixth round trips the arbiter.** `scripts/hooks/lib/hm_review_round.py` already numbers a spec
review's rounds (the counter back to one when a round returns FAITHFUL, and a new pass for an amendment). Where it computes
the round, before the snapshot moves (so a refused dispatch spends nothing), a round past `SPEC_ROUND_CAP = 5` beyond the
`continue` rulings on this PASS of the review, `round:spec-fidelity|<feature>#<pass>@` (the pass counted beside the
round in `.git/review-round/<feature>/pass`, one more each time a dispatch follows an ACCEPTED pass - a FAITHFUL round, or
the arbiter's `accept` or `process-fault` on that pass, which accept the spec as FAITHFUL does - so a ruling on one pass
neither lifts nor closes a later pass's cap; plan review rounds 1 and 2; a `REVIEW_ROUND_OK` full re-read after an accepted
pass starts the new pass too, found when amendment 3's first round counted as round 4), trips that trigger (`hm_arbiter.trip`, kind `round`) and refuses
with `hm_arbiter.refusal`, as `pair-hooks.sh` does for a review check's third round; `ARBITER_OK="<reason>"` in the prompt
is the escape (the hook's own census row). An `accept` or `process-fault` ruling closes the pass: it accepts the spec as FAITHFUL does, so the next dispatch is an
amendment's new pass at round 1.

**D12 - An `accept` or `process-fault` is the spec's verdict at the push.** `review-gate.sh` refuses a spec with no
FAITHFUL verdict; an arbiter's `accept` or `process-fault` on the review, `round:spec-fidelity|<feature>#<pass>@N` in that
feature's tracked `arbiter.jsonl`, answers it only while the spec reads as it did when ruled: the ruling row carries
`spec_sha`, the hash of what the review judged - `spec.md`'s title and everything from its first `## ` heading to its
Review history, the header block between them dropped WHOLE, so a Status line rewritten at landing (one line or wrapped onto
two) keeps the ruling while a requirement edit cancels it (plan review rounds 3 and 4; `hm_arbiter.spec_body_sha`) - and the
gate asks
`hm_arbiter.py spec-ruled` - no untracked per-clone state, so any clone's push of an amended spec is refused on an old
ruling (plan review round 2). A `continue` does not answer it (the spec stands as
the last round left it, the GM reviewing the ruling after landing). Without it, "accept" would leave the feature unable to
land - the stop the GM asked to remove.

**D13 - One command for any other process stop.** `make arbiter-ask SUBJECT=<short id> WHY="<the question>"` trips
`ask:<subject>` (kind `ask`, the question its detail; the escape floor on WHY) and builds its bundle in the same command,
printing the MANIFEST to dispatch `round-arbiter` on (FR-009's one command). It holds nothing - the session asked because it is stuck - and the ruling lands on the GM's review like any other. The
round arbiter's contract gains what each ruling means for a spec review (continue: one more round; accept: the spec
stands; process-fault: the review loop is the fault, its `tooling_fix`) and for an `ask` (continue: go on as the question
proposed - for a regression, fix it; accept: it stands, waived; process-fault: the process is wrong, its `tooling_fix`). The bundle states, for a
spec review, that its rounds are the spec's Review history (copied beside it), and for an `ask`, the question.

**D14 - The cap and the exits written once, as five and the arbiter.** The spec-review cap reads five rounds, then the
round arbiter, in CLAUDE.md, the constitution's XVI (its "STOP and put it to the GM" and the two stale sentences counting
three), `.claude/agents/spec-fidelity.md` and `spec-fidelity-verify.md`, and `docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md`;
`review-gate.sh`'s two-round message is the review checks' cap and stays. The regression exit's "explicit GM waiver"
(CLAUDE.md, `docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md`, the constitution's XIII) becomes the round arbiter's ruling through `make
arbiter-ask`, reviewed by the GM after landing. The stop-and-ask rule (CLAUDE.md, `docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md`) is split
as FR-009 says - how the process goes to the arbiter first, what to build to the GM - and so are `wakeup-hooks.sh`'s two
"a question for the GM" lines and `escalation-check.md`'s "a question or a decision" for the GM.

**D15 - The GM's-words waiver of a review check's cap is retired (FR-010).** `pair-hooks.sh` drops its `REVIEW_ROUNDS_OK`
branch, so a third round past the cap meets only the arbiter path (the refusal naming `make arbiter-bundle`); its census
entry in `tests/tooling/test_guard_firing_log.py` goes, its suite's waiver cases become a refusal case, and
`docs/reviews.md`'s sentence names the arbiter. The event log's `waiver` flag stays, reading old transcripts.

## Amendment 3 - the band-3 sign-off to the arbiter (FR-011)

**D16 - A band-3 increase is an `ask` the push reads.** `make perf-arbiter [ENV=]` takes the pair's subject from
`perf_review.py arbiter-subject` - `perf-band3-<environment>-<first 12 of the pair's binding>`, so the question is bound to
that commit, environment and those exact percentages - and runs `make arbiter-ask` with it (D13: the trigger recorded and
the bundle built in one command), writing `perf_review.py show`'s report beside the MANIFEST as `perf-report.txt`. Only a
band-3 pair has a subject. `perf_review.check` counts an arbiter `accept` on `ask:<that subject>` in the feature's
`arbiter.jsonl` as the band-3 record (`arbiter_signed`); `continue`, `process-fault` and a ruling on other numbers do not
(a new pair has a new subject). The push's MISSING line names `make perf-arbiter` alone, "never a question to the GM"; the
`signoff` command stays only to record a sign-off the GM gives unprompted, in their words, and its refusal names the
arbiter. The arbiter's contract states the band-3 standard it rules by. Every text FR-011 lists says the arbiter:
`perf_bands.py`'s table and the band-3 line every report prints, `perf_review.py`'s docstring and both refusals,
`perf_snapshot.py`'s comment, `perf-audit.md`'s band-3 section, the constitution's band table, `dev/performance.md`,
`docs/guards.md`, `l7r/diagram/CLAUDE.md`, `sync-with-main.sh`'s comment, the Makefile's comment and `perf-signoff` help.
The session memory that told sessions to ask the GM's go-ahead is rewritten (outside the repository). `perf_review.py` is engine code under the 100% floor: its tests carry both functions.

## Tasks

T01 the field, the record, `open_fixes`, the found row retired (D1, D2); T02 the holds (D3) and the two commands (D4, D5);
T03 the contract; T04 tests red on today's code, the replay (D6), the docs (D7); T05 the gate, the report, landed.

decisions.summary: Optional `tooling_fix` field (one sentence); contract gives one whenever the judged loop came from a tooling gap and says it is made, never filed; record_ruling refuses a process-fault without one; 'filed as a tooling row' replaced by 'the fault is your tooling_fix'.
decisions.why: FR-001 verbatim: the field, when to give one, process-fault always carries its fault, no 'file a tooling row'. The refusal on a process-fault without the field only enforces FR-001. 'Whenever the loop came from a tooling gap' is a floor (must give one then), not a ceiling; the contract must keep FR-001's 'never only in its prose' for any tooling fix the arbiter recommends, or an incidental one is lost again. The accept line's 'filed as rows' concerns finding rows, not tooling rows, and FR-001 does not reach it. (Text unchanged since the CLEAR plan review of D1-D10; re-confirmed against amendment 2's spec, which adds FR-007 to FR-010 and narrows none of D1-D10.) Unchanged in plan rounds 2 to 5; carried forward. Text unchanged by amendment 3; carried forward (amendment 3 adds FR-011 and narrows none of it).

decisions.summary: record_ruling keeps tooling_fix on the arbiter.jsonl row with fix:open and on the GM-review row; later fix_of rows close it, latest wins; open_fixes() is the one rule; the process-fault found.jsonl row is no longer written.
decisions.why: FR-002: recorded as an open item of the active feature, the GM-review row carries it. Retiring the found.jsonl row narrows nothing: grep finds no reader of found.jsonl in scripts/ (only writers: hm_arbiter.py:218, gm_review.py:116, record_owed.py:344), so the row was unenforced, and FR-001 puts the process-fault's fault into tooling_fix, held and shown to the GM like any other. (Text unchanged since the CLEAR plan review of D1-D10; re-confirmed against amendment 2's spec, which adds FR-007 to FR-010 and narrows none of D1-D10.) decisions.why: FR-002 'made, with its test' and 'adds what was built and its test to that review'. The TEST requirement only enforces 'with its test' and cannot exclude a legitimate fix: guard companions live under tests/hooks/ (Makefile hooks-test), so every test kind sits under tests/. decisions.why: FR-003 as written: an overhaul declined to the GM's review, never filed, never a stop-and-ask. Overturn into a feature is the GM's existing gm_review power, not a session filing. (Text unchanged since the CLEAR plan review of D1-D10; re-confirmed against amendment 2's spec, which adds FR-007 to FR-010 and narrows none of D1-D10.) decisions.why: SC-001 asks for a replay, and this is one, covering every clause of it. Not writing the historical ruling back as a live open item narrows nothing: the fix is made (scripts/gates/gate_lock.py and tests/tooling/test_gate_lock.py exist, commit 8bc9db0c1), and the GM knows of it ('the one that we are doing now for making sure that make done cannot be run twice'). decisions.summary: The open-task refusal is not touched (no flag); make land-tooling FILES= builds a new commit on the latest main holding only FILES' committed changes since the merge base (git diff base HEAD -- FILES, git apply --index, a failure being 'does not apply cleanly'), in a detached worktree at .clones/<clone>-tooling, landed by the sync script's stop-work step run from the worktree so every push check runs; clone history untouched; worktree removed on every exit.
decisions.why: FR-005: the tooling lands on main by itself, on top of the latest main, through a push's checks, no history rewritten, no local branch, while the feature's other work stays in the clone (the refusal is meant to keep holding it - SC-003 'the full push is still refused'). The request's 'a commit that touches only tooling land on its own' is the accepted spec's 'lands a commit's TOOLING'; a new commit of that tooling on main is that, not less. Measured premises checked: .specify/feature.json is gitignored (.gitignore:124, not in ls-files), and the sync script derives the active feature only from touched specs/ and that pointer (lines 415-422) and checks only that its root is under .clones/ (line 65), so the push from the worktree finds no feature in progress. (Text unchanged since the CLEAR plan review of D1-D10; re-confirmed against amendment 2's spec, which adds FR-007 to FR-010 and narrows none of D1-D10.) Unchanged in plan rounds 2 to 5; carried forward. Text unchanged by amendment 3; carried forward (amendment 3 adds FR-011 and narrows none of it).

decisions.summary: FILES is required and named (none given: list the changed tooling paths, exit 2); a path outside FR-005's set refused naming it; a FILE with uncommitted changes refused; a Makefile regenerates docs/make-targets.html; before the push: make hooks-test, make test-file FILE=tests/tooling, and make test-file on each test file among FILES, in the worktree, logged; commit with the GM's identity, the clone's subjects, the co-author line.
decisions.why: The path set is FR-005's list exactly (scripts/, tests/, .claude/agents/, .claude/skills/, any CLAUDE.md, Makefile, .claude/settings.json, docs/make-targets.html), refused 'naming it' as FR-005 says. Naming the files withholds nothing the GM asked to land: any tooling path may be named, and the no-FILES case prints the compliant command. 'Only committed work' is FR-005's 'a commit's tooling'. Running each landed test before the push is FR-005's 'any test it lands is run there ... refused rather than breaking main' and SC-003's last clause; hooks-test and tests/tooling are the checks this project owes a tooling change before it lands (Constitution XIII, the plan's own constitution check) and enforce 'rather than breaking main', so they serve the request rather than add scope. Regenerating make-targets.html is the wiring FR-005 names. (Text unchanged since the CLEAR plan review of D1-D10; re-confirmed against amendment 2's spec, which adds FR-007 to FR-010 and narrows none of D1-D10.) decisions.summary: hm_review_round.py: a spec review's round past SPEC_ROUND_CAP=5 plus the continue rulings on THIS PASS (round:spec-fidelity|<feature>#<pass>@) trips @N and refuses before the snapshot moves; the pass advances when a dispatch follows an ACCEPTED pass - a FAITHFUL round, or the arbiter's accept or process-fault on that pass (ruled_closed); ARBITER_OK escape. Amendment 3: a REVIEW_ROUND_OK full re-read after an ACCEPTED pass also starts the new pass at round 1 (accepted_pass).
decisions.why: Within. The pass advancing on FAITHFUL or on the arbiter's accept/process-fault is FR-007's 'counter reset when a spec is accepted or amended'; ARBITER_OK follows the pair-hooks precedent FR-007 names. Amendment 3's added note: the escape path now does what the routed path already did - accepted_pass() resets to round 1 and advances the pass only when the last pass ended FAITHFUL (transcript, else the Review history) or closed by an arbiter accept/process-fault; otherwise it keeps the round as before. That is FR-007's reset applied to the one path that skipped it (amendment 3's own first round had counted as round 4 of a finished pass), neither lifting a cap mid-pass nor adding one. Test: tests/hooks/test-review-round-hooks.sh section 10 (round 3 + FAITHFUL + escape -> round 1, pass 3). Round 3's note (b) stands as an aside.

decisions.summary: An arbiter accept/process-fault answers review-gate.sh in place of FAITHFUL only while spec.md's title and its sections up to the Review history hash as when ruled (header block dropped whole); a continue does not.
decisions.why: Round 4's item resolved. spec_body_sha now hashes the title line plus everything from the first '## ' heading to the Review history, the header block between dropped whole (head.split('\n',1)[0] + sep + rest). MEASURED on round 5's own run, 2026-10-10: on a copy of 379's own spec.md, Status rewritten to a Done that wraps onto a second line keeps the hash (True); a one-word FR-007 edit changes it (False). tests/hooks/test-review-gate.sh: 38 passed 0 failed (b4's new two-line Status case among them); tests/tooling/test_arbiter_fix.py: 9 passed (the spec-ruling test now writes a wrapped Status and keeps the ruling; the requirement edit still cancels). The remaining narrowing - a requirement edit cancels the ruling - is LEGITIMATE: implied by FR-007's own 'counter reset when a spec is accepted or amended' (an amended spec owes a new review, not an old ruling), and it applies to the requirements only, so an arbiter-accepted feature lands with its Status rewritten (D12's own purpose). Aside, not a finding: a spec with no '## ' heading hashes its title alone (3 of the repository's specs, all filed/withdrawn/done stubs: 275, 325, 373), so a body edit there keeps a ruling - that is looser, never stricter, than the request, and the FAITHFUL path (a grep over spec.md) is not content-bound at all. Text unchanged by amendment 3; carried forward (amendment 3 adds FR-011 and narrows none of it).

decisions.summary: make arbiter-ask SUBJECT= WHY= trips `ask:<subject>` (kind ask, escape floor on WHY) and builds its bundle in the same command, printing the MANIFEST; holds nothing; the contract gains each ruling's meaning for a spec review and for an ask (continue on a regression: fix it); the bundle states the spec's Review history or the question.
decisions.why: FR-009's 'one command that records the question as a trigger and builds its bundle': the plan now says so and the Makefile recipe chains `hm_arbiter.py ask` and `scripts/reviews/arbiter_bundle.py "ask:$(SUBJECT)" --root` (argparse takes the trigger positionally and --root). 'Holds nothing' is within (FR-009 asks for no hold). The ruling meanings follow FR-007 and FR-008, including FR-008's continue = fix it for a regression, now in the plan text. Round 1's item resolved. Unchanged in plan rounds 3 to 5; carried forward. Text unchanged by amendment 3; carried forward (amendment 3 adds FR-011 and narrows none of it).

decisions.summary: The spec-review cap reads five rounds then the round arbiter in CLAUDE.md, the constitution's XVI (and its two stale 'three' sentences), both fidelity agent files and docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md; review-gate.sh's two-round message stays; the regression exit's GM waiver becomes the arbiter's ruling via arbiter-ask (CLAUDE.md, the doc, XIII); the stop-and-ask rule, wakeup-hooks.sh's two lines and escalation-check.md split as FR-009 says.
decisions.why: Clause for clause the file lists of FR-007 and SC-006, including the review checks' two-round cap staying; feature approval, content questions and renaming stay with the GM as the spec reserves them. Corrected for amendment 3: the band-3 sign-off is no longer reserved (FR-011, D16 carries it); D14's own text never mentioned band 3, so it narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: pair-hooks.sh drops its REVIEW_ROUNDS_OK branch so a third round past the cap meets only the arbiter path; its census entry and waiver cases become a refusal case; docs/reviews.md names the arbiter; the event log's waiver flag stays for old transcripts.
decisions.why: FR-010 verbatim: the GM's-words waiver retired, its refusal naming the arbiter route; SC-006's REVIEW_ROUNDS_OK refused naming the arbiter. Keeping the event log able to read old transcripts adds no behavior. (Aside for implementation: pair-hooks.sh line 522's comment still says the third round 'needs REVIEW_ROUNDS_OK'.) Unchanged in plan rounds 3 to 5; carried forward. Text unchanged by amendment 3; carried forward (amendment 3 adds FR-011 and narrows none of it).

decisions.summary: make perf-arbiter [ENV=] takes subject perf-band3-<env>-<first 12 of binding(commit, environment, measurements)> from perf_review.py arbiter-subject (band 3 only) and runs make arbiter-ask, writing perf_review show's report beside the MANIFEST; perf_review.check counts an arbiter accept on ask:<that subject> in the feature's arbiter.jsonl as the band-3 record; continue, process-fault and other numbers do not; the MISSING line names perf-arbiter alone, 'never a question to the GM'; signoff stays only for a sign-off the GM gives unprompted, its no-terminal refusal naming the arbiter; the arbiter's contract states the standard it rules by (the band-2 criteria, held strictest); every FR-011 text says the arbiter; the session memory is rewritten.
decisions.why: FR-011 clause by clause. 'One command that records the question and builds its bundle, the perf report in it': perf-arbiter chains arbiter-ask (hm_arbiter ask + arbiter_bundle) and writes perf-report.txt to /tmp/l7r-check/arbiter-ask-<subject>, which is the bundle's own directory (arbiter_bundle slug of 'ask:perf-band3-...' is 'ask-perf-band3-...', 37 chars, under its 60 cut). 'An accept bound to that bookend pair's exact numbers': the subject is the pair's existing binding (sha256 of commit, environment, measurements), so new numbers mean a new trigger. 'continue and process-fault do not; a ruling on other numbers is stale': arbiter_signed matches ruling == accept on the exact trigger only; tests/tools/test_perf_review.py test_band_3_goes_to_the_round_arbiter_first covers continue, other numbers and accept. 'The push's refusal names that command alone': the MISSING line names make perf-arbiter and not perf-signoff (asserted). 'A sign-off the GM gives unprompted still counts': signoff --tty yes still records and passes check (test_band_3_a_GM_signoff_given_unprompted_is_still_recorded). The push wiring reaches it: sync-with-main runs make perf-review, i.e. check with --specs-dir defaulting to the repository's specs/, and record_ruling writes the accept into the active feature's tracked arbiter.jsonl, the file arbiter_signed reads. Giving the arbiter a standard to rule by narrows nothing the GM asked: FR-011 puts the decision to the arbiter, and a stated standard is how it decides; the GM reviews every ruling after landing. 'Only band 3 has a subject' is FR-011's scope (band 3 only). The memory rewrite serves 'the session NEVER asks the GM'.
